reviews.title: Terrible Customer Service for Decent AI Tool
reviews.text:
Pollo AI actually seems like a pretty impressive app at first. The video generation is decent, the ideas translate well, and it looks like it has a lot of potential.

Unfortunately, that’s where the positive experience ends.

This app feels like a money trap disguised as a creative tool. You’ll spend time building a project, getting invested in the process, and then suddenly get hit with a message saying you don’t have enough credits to continue. Fine. You assume you just need to buy more credits to finish what you’ve already started.

So I purchased 300 additional credits for $17.99.

Guess what happened next?

I went right back to my project and got the exact same error message saying I still didn’t have enough credits. At no point does the app clearly tell you how many credits are required to complete your project. Are you short by 10 credits? 100? 1,000? Nobody knows.

And customer service is absolutely useless. You can send screenshots, receipts, proof of purchase—everything they ask for—and they still act like the credits you paid for somehow don’t matter. Instead of resolving the issue, they just send canned responses while your project sits unfinished.

So now I’m out money, I still can’t complete my project, and I still have no idea how many credits are actually required.

The technology itself may be good, but the billing and credit system is incredibly misleading and frustrating. Save yourself the headache, save yourself the money, and don’t waste your time downloa

reviews.title: Deceptive pricing, double monetization, and broken credits system
reviews.text:
I subscribed to this app because the onboarding and description clearly suggest that a subscription allows you to create videos.
In reality, the subscription gives you almost nothing, and you are required to buy additional credits inside the app just to generate a video.

But it gets worse.

I currently have 120 credits, and creating a video costs exactly 120 credits.
Despite this, the app does not allow me to create the video and instead forces me to a screen where I’m asked to buy more credits, as if I don’t have enough. This is either a critical bug or an intentional manipulation.

Summary:
	•	✔️ Subscription paid
	•	✔️ Credits available
	•	❌ Video creation blocked
	•	❌ Constant pressure to buy more credits

This is a clear example of double (or even triple) monetization combined with dark UX patterns. Users are misled into paying multiple times just to access basic functionality.

If you’re considering a subscription — don’t.
Until the developers clearly explain what the subscription is actually for, and fix the broken credits logic, this app is effectively unusable.

Very disappointing. Not recommended.
